display.title: Episode 326: The Silver-Coated Mirror (Pesach Sheni)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi explains that Tzivos Hashem's only battle is against the yetzer hara, teaches that Pesach Sheni means it's never too late, and tells of a generous man whom riches turned into a miser.
display.summary_long: Broadcast on 16 Iyar 5748, between Pesach Sheni and Lag BaOmer. Uncle Yossi describes Tzivos Hashem as a living peace corps whose only enemy is the yetzer hara, the inner voice that pushes us to do wrong and makes us lazy about mitzvos; the only weapons against it are Torah, mitzvos and good midos. He explains how to join Tzivos Hashem and earn points with mitzvah charts. Then he teaches about Pesach Sheni, the second chance Hashem gave to bring the Korban Pesach, and the Rebbe's lesson that it is never too late to become better, even when the yetzer hara says otherwise. Two brothers visit Studio 604 to lead the Shema. Story time tells of Reb Avraham, a kind man who gave tzedakah generously and asked a visiting Rebbe for a blessing of wealth. As his business grew, he stopped davening in shul, learning and welcoming the poor. A year later the Rebbe returns and shows him the difference between a window and a mirror: once glass is coated with silver, you see only yourself. Reb Avraham does teshuvah and becomes generous again. The show ends with a sponsor message and the Lag BaOmer parade.
display.lesson: Riches are a blessing only if we share them; and like Pesach Sheni, it is never too late to do teshuvah and return to our good ways.
